subtitle: Keep the features that earn their place. Drop the rest.

steps.label: OVERFITTING & SPEED
steps.sub: Fewer ways to memorize noise; faster, cheaper

steps.label: INTERPRETABILITY & ROBUSTNESS
steps.sub: 8 inputs beats 800; fewer pipelines to break

eyebrow: A filter example: diabetes dataset, 10 features
code:
kb = SelectKBest(f_regression, k=4).fit(X, y)
print(dict(zip(X.columns, kb.scores_.round(1))))
# bmi 230.7, s5 207.3 (highest) ... sex 0.8 (barely registers)
caption: f_regression ranks each feature on its own relationship to the target.

code:
# filter (top 4):  ['bmi', 'bp', 's4', 's5']
rfe = RFE(LinearRegression(), n_features_to_select=4).fit(X, y)
print(list(X.columns[rfe.support_]))
# wrapper (RFE):    ['bmi', 's1', 's2', 's5']
caption: s1 and s2 are correlated -- the wrapper judges them jointly; the filter scores each alone.

steps.label: FILTERS ASK: USEFUL ALONE?
steps.sub: One feature at a time, independently

eyebrow: Avoiding leakage: put the selector in a pipeline
code:
pipe = make_pipeline(SelectKBest(f_regression, k=4), LinearRegression())
cross_val_score(pipe, X, y, cv=5, scoring="r2").mean()
caption: Refit on the training portion of EVERY fold -- selecting on the whole dataset first would leak.

code:
# 4 selected features: mean R² = 0.46
# all 10 features:     mean R² = 0.482
caption: Four features recover most of the performance -- a useful trade, but not a guarantee.
